title: Managing financial risk

draft.title: Managing financial risk
card: Financial risk is the chance of losing money or not reaching a money goal. People cannot remove it, but they can reduce it.
A financial goal is a target, such as saving $2000 for a laptop in a year. A goal helps a person plan what to spend and what to put aside.
Savings are money set aside to cover surprise costs, such as a broken phone. Insurance means paying a fee so an insurer covers a large loss, such as a car crash or a house fire.
Before paying or sharing details, check who is asking. Contact the business through an official number or website you already trust, not the link or number in the message.
draft.remember: Goals, savings, insurance and checking first each reduce the chance that a money problem becomes a big loss.

a.q: Liam pays a yearly fee to an insurer. How does this help him manage financial risk?
opts: The insurer covers a large loss if it happens
It stops the loss from ever happening
It adds to his savings for surprise costs
It sets a target for how much he will spend
a.why: Insurance moves the cost of a large loss to the insurer in return for a fee. It does not stop the loss happening, and the fee is not savings that Liam can use for other costs.
a.clue: Think about who pays when the big loss happens.

b.q: Priya gets a text saying her bank account is locked, with a link to log in. What is the best way to manage the risk?
opts: Call the bank on the number from its official website
Use the link quickly so the account is not closed
Reply to the text and ask if the message is real
Log in through the link and then change her password
b.why: Contacting the bank through a number she already trusts checks who is really asking. Using the link or replying to the text still relies on the message, which may come from someone pretending to be the bank.
b.clue: Where should the contact details come from?

a.best: The insurer covers a large loss if it happens

b.best: Call the bank on the number from its official website
